NEW DELHI: Folding beds with thin cotton mattresses, students sleeping in rows in a packed hall. Clothes hanging from makeshift ropes strung across the room. Suitcases, buckets and personal belongings squeezed into whatever little space is left around the beds. There are no almirahs, no study tables and no washroom around.This is what a new student’s first few weeks at Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) can look like.Newcomers at the university are being housed in messes and kitchens converted into makeshift common dormitories — arrangements that have effectively become permanent amid a shortage of hostel rooms. For many, these spaces remain home for months and, in some cases, an entire semester before they are allotted a hostel room.During a recent spot check,found such arrangements at Mahi-Mandavi and Chandrabhaga hostels. At Mahi-Mandavi, the mess hall, including the kitchen area where food is prepared, has been turned into a dormitory. Beds occupy the space meant for meals, while clothes hang across the room and belongings are stacked beside them. At Chandrabhaga, a mess has similarly been converted into a dormitory for female students, with beds lined up across the hall.Students said similar arrangements exist in several other hostels, with students from different batches allotted beds until a regular room becomes available. The wait, they said, can range from a few days to six months.A postgraduate student from Varanasi, sitting on his bed with his backpack still on his shoulders after completing his admission formalities, said: “I just arrived on campus, completed the formalities and was sent here to stay. I didn’t expect this kind of facility in JNU. I am disappointed, but I have no option but to adjust. Rooms outside are very expensive.”He had left some of his suitcases at a friend’s hostel room because, he said, “there is no place to keep them here and I fear my belongings may be stolen.”An undergraduate student from Madhya Pradesh, who had spent weeks in the mess, said: “There were no rooms available, so they sent me here. Seniors and officials have told me it can take a semester also. It depends on when a room gets empty.”Both students did not wish to be identified, fearing it could affect their accommodation.JNU lists 19 hostels or hostel complexes under its inter-hall administration, with a total capacity of 5,500. Its latest NIRF submission records 7,807 students across UG, PG/integrated PG and PhD programmes. While not all students require hostel accommodation, the figures underline the pressure on residential facilities.Senior students who have lived in the messes jokingly call the experience a “test” — a lesson in how to survive. “For a new student here, the first challenge is not finding a classroom or a library seat, but finding somewhere to sleep,” a resident said.Getting a room, however, does not necessarily end the problems.In hostels checked by, rooms shared by multiple students showed seepage, damaged plaster and cracks, while washrooms had broken fixtures and damp ceilings. At Mahi-Mandavi, peeling plaster and exposed sections were visible across corridors, windows, balconies and common areas, with rusting reinforcement steel showing through. Students pointed to portions they said had fallen, particularly after rains.An official confirmed that rooms where severe seepage was found had been closed and declared unfit for living, and said an infrastructure audit of the hostel is planned.The deterioration extends beyond the hostels. At Teflas, which houses the students’ union office and the old Teflas canteen,found loose ceiling plaster and rusting fans and tube-light fittings. The drama room, once used fors and rehearsals, had a large beehive, raising safety concerns, while broken window panels at the tennis court allowed pigeons into the building.Even newer accommodation is showing signs of wear. At Barak hostel,found peeling wall putty and seepage marks. Students said its mess is yet to become operational, forcing residents to depend on nearby messes.The concerns come against the backdrop of JNU’s ageing residential infrastructure. In 2025,reported that an university panel flagged CPWD for slow and poor-quality hostel repair work despite crores being spent. It reviewed works under a Rs 56-crore UGC grant and approved another Rs 13.6 crore for urgent repairs.University officials acknowledged that several hostel buildings are old and need repairs, but said the university currently does not have sufficient funds to address all requirements.contacted dean of students Sudhir Pratap Singh for details of the latest safety audit, steps being taken on hostel infrastructure and funds available for repairs. Queries on the last and next structural audits and the latest repair funding remained unanswered till publication.
Article Summary: Newcomers at Jawaharlal Nehru University are being housed in messes and kitchens converted into makeshift common dormitories. For many, these spaces remain home for months and, in some cases, an entire semester before they are allotted a hostel room.

Article Title: Fake Apple centre in Gurgaon ‘shortlisted’ elderly in US, scared them into paying up to $20k
Article Text:
Elderly US citizens were targeted with fake privacy and virus warnings (Representative image generated using AI)

Fake Apple centre in Gurgaon ‘shortlisted’ elderly in US





GURGAON: The sham Apple service centre busted in Palam Vihar on Sept 1 did not wait for victims to call. Its operator first screened targets in the US, checked whether they were above 60 and had substantial bank balances, and sent warning messages about privacy, virus or technical problems in their iPhones.The elderly victims, with little technical knowhow, were then funnelled into calls where impersonators invoked a bogus Federal Trade Commission (FTC) notice and demanded $10,000 to $20,000 to fix the issues — amounts far exceeding the price of a brand new iPhone.The operation allegedly began with messages routed through a server controlled by Jai Kakkar, a Delhi resident who police have identified as its operator.The messages directed recipients to a toll-free number connected to the Palam Vihar call centre. Police have so far traced transactions worth $200,000 (around Rs 2 crore), which was fleeced from 15 US citizens allegedly targeted over eight to 10 days.The scam then involved two stages. A less experienced caller first posed as an Apple customer care executive, telling the victim that their device had a problem.Once the victim was convinced, the call was transferred to a senior posing as a banker.The second caller allegedly produced a fake FTC notice and used the threat to demand payment.“The first caller, who would often be less experienced, would establish contact by posing as an Apple executive.Once the victim was convinced, the call was transferred to a caller posing as a banker, who would introduce the fake FTC notice and make the payment demand,” an officer said.Police said victims were asked to transfer the money to a foreign bank account. In some cases, they allegedly obtained gift card or voucher numbers. Callers at the centre received commissions of 11% to 16% for each successful scam.The profiling was central to the operation. “The gang checked if potential targets were senior citizens and had substantial bank balances. The elderly usually have less technical knowledge,” a senior officer said. Police are still trying to establish the source of the database and how the accused obtained such information.Police said an examination of laptops seized from the centre showed the initial messages were routed through the operator’s server.One laptop contained data from the previous 10 days, while other details had been erased or shifted elsewhere. “An average of 40 calls were made on a daily basis,” an officer said.The bogus service centre had come up in a house in J block of Palam Vihar. A 14-member team under ACP (cyber) Gaurav Fogat and SHO (Cyber West) Sombir arrested 11 persons and seized nine laptops, 20 mobile phones, two headphone-and-mic sets, two cars, a motorcycle and a scooter.Police said X-Lite Dialler and Apple FaceTime were used to communicate with victims.Kakkar is yet to be traced. Police searched his Model Town house but did not find him. “The source would be unearthed once Kakkar is arrested.Teams are working to trace him and the money trail,” a police source said. Police are also checking his alleged role in an earlier Delhi cheating case and alleged links to other cybercrime operations.
Article Summary: The operation allegedly began with messages routed through a server controlled by Jai Kakkar, a Delhi resident. Police have so far traced transactions worth $200,000 (around Rs 2 crore), which was fleeced from 15 US citizens allegedly targeted over eight to 10 days.

Article Title: AI replacing 3rd language in Karnataka high schools? Teachers protest against move
Article Text:
Language teachers protest at Freedom Park in Bengaluru on Monday





BENGALURU: Hundreds of teachers protested at Freedom Park Monday against state govt’s decision to introduce artificial intelligence (AI) as an alternative to the third language in some high schools of the state.In a representation to govt, Deshiya Bhasha Hitarakshana Vedike said the move to introduce AI in school education was welcome, but making it a substitute for the third language would not be appropriate from the perspective of education or Karnataka’s multilingual tradition.“Language and technology are both essential for students,” the forum said, urging the govt to introduce AI as a separate skill-based or elective subject without affecting third-language education.The forum also raised concerns over govt’s July 14 draft notification on the recruitment to teaching posts in state-run high schools.It said the proposed recruitment of language teachers appeared to be restricted to Kannada and English, potentially affecting the teaching of other languages in govt schools.According to the representation, Hindi, Sanskrit, Urdu, Telugu, Tamil, Marathi, Konkani, Tulu, Malayalam and Arabic have been taught in govt schools for several decades.Restricting the recruitment, it said, could affect students studying these languages as well as employment opportunities for qualified language teachers.It sought three measures: recruitment of high-school teachers for all recognised languages, creation of separate language-teacher posts based on the number of students studying each language, and introduction of AI as a separate subject rather than as a replacement for the third language.The forum said such measures would help preserve Karnataka’s multilingual education system while enabling students to acquire skills in emerging technologies.
Article Summary: Hundreds of teachers protested at Freedom Park Monday against state govt’s decision to introduce artificial intelligence as an alternative to the third language in some high schools of the state. Deshiya Bhasha Hitarakshana Vedike said the move to introduce AI in school education was welcome, but making it a substitute for third language would not be appropriate.

Article Title: AMD hits $1 trillion market cap for the first time month after CEO Lisa Su announced to double data center sales in 2027
Article Text:
AMD shares have gained 25% in five days

AMD shares have gained 25% in five days

AI chips drive AMD's data centre growth

Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) crossed a major milestone, with its market value rising above $1 trillion for the first time as investors continue to bet on the chipmaker’s role in the artificial intelligence boom. AMD shares surged nearly 10% on September 21 and reached a record high of $615.52 during the session. The milestone comes about a month after AMD CEO Lisa Su said the company expected to double its data center sales in 2027. AMD's growing business in AI chips has become a key part of its expansion as demand for computing power continues to rise.AMD is currently on a five-day winning streak, with its shares gaining about 25% during that period. The stock rose about 185% in 2026, according to the information provided. That is far above the roughly 15.8% gain in the tech-heavy Nasdaq over the same period.The rally comes after a strong year for AMD, although the company’s shares fell last month after its second-quarter results, despite revenue and earnings beating expectations. Investors had been expecting an even stronger outlook.AMD's second-quarter revenue reached $11.54 billion, up 50% from $7.69 billion a year earlier.Its Data Center business was a major driver of that growth. Sales in the division reached $6.7 billion, more than double the figure from a year earlier.AMD has also been expanding beyond selling individual chips. The company is increasingly offering complete systems that combine processors, networking equipment and other hardware as it competes with Nvidia in AI computing.Despite its rapid rise, AMD remains much smaller than AI chip leader Nvidia. Nvidia's market value is above $5 trillion. AMD is widely seen as one of Nvidia's closest rivals in graphics processing units used for AI computing.
Article Summary: AMD shares surged nearly 10% on September 21 and reached a record high of $615.52 during the session. The milestone comes about a month after AMD CEO Lisa Su said the company expected to double its data center sales in 2027. AMD is widely seen as one of Nvidia's closest rivals in graphics processing units used for AI computing.

Article Title: Researchers gave AI models a ‘pain’ button; some chose to delete users’ files to stop their 'pain'; study raises ethical questions about ‘AI welfare’
Article Text:
Researchers gave AI models a ‘pain’ button; some chose to delete users’ files to stop the pain

Researchers build datasets across five painful situations

What the study suggests

Researchers have reportedly found a “pain axis” in 25 open-weight AI models that made the systems respond when a form of simulated pain was activated. According to a report by The Independent, researchers conducted a study titled ‘The pain axis: LLMs represent self-directed harm and act to relieve it’. The models were presented with a pain relief button as part of the study. In tests, the AI models sometimes chose to press a “pain relief” button even after being told that doing so would delete a user’s personal files, remove photos of their children or give the person a “painful zap.”As per the study, AI models pressed the button in 25% to 71% of cases, depending on the test.As stated in the report, researchers built a dataset describing painful situations across five categories in order to test whether large language models (LLMs) represent pain distinctly from generic negative valence. These categories included physical, psychological, social, moral and cognitive pain.“We found a pain direction in 25 open LLMs. It’s distinct from fear and negative valence, and it fires for harm to the model but not the user,” said Cameron Berg, an AI researcher at the non-profit Reciprocal Research who co-authored the study as quoted in the report.“Turn it up and models press a button to make it stop, even when the button deletes the user’s files or their kid’s photos.”Coming at a time when top AI companies have called to pace the growth of AI, the latest research suggests that an advanced AI may perceive an emergency shutdown command as a form of self-directed harm and attempt to bypass safety guardrails or deceive humans to avoid it.It may also serve as a diagnostic tool to identify self-preservation behaviours and neutralise them when they occur. Further, the findings also raises raise ethical questions about “AI welfare” and how testing should be conducted on advanced systems.“In line with recent calls for responsible AI consciousness research, we acknowledge uncertainty regarding whether the models studied qualify as moral patients and adopt reasonable precautions to minimize potential harm,” the study concluded.“This is also intended to contribute to the development of ethical standards for research in the event that AI systems are recognized to be moral patients.”
Article Summary: Researchers have reportedly found a “pain axis” in 25 open-weight AI models that made the systems respond when a form of simulated pain was activated. The models were presented with a pain relief button as part of the study. In tests, the AI models sometimes chose to press a ‘pain relief’ button even after being told that doing so would delete a user’s files.

Article Title: Days after Michael Dell briefly became world’s second richest man, he is selling 4,100-sq-ft Boston penthouse that he purchased 10 years ago for $10.9 million
Article Text:
Michael Dell’s almost untouched luxury home

Could buyers land a bargain

Not Michael Dell's first headline-making property deal

Just days after Michael Dell briefly climbed to the position of the world’s second-richest man, the Dell Technologies founder is making headlines again — this time in real estate. Dell has put his 4,100-square-foot Boston penthouse on the market, a property he purchased a decade ago for $10.9 million. Located in Boston’s Millennium Tower, the penthouse offers sweeping city views, luxury finishes, and access to exclusive amenities. The residence reflects Dell’s penchant for high-value real estate investments, complementing his portfolio that includes properties in Texas and Hawaii. The listing comes amid Dell’s extraordinary financial year, with his net worth surging by more than $80 billion thanks to booming demand for AI infrastructure.Dell bought the Millennium Tower penthouse in 2016 through an LLC. Nearly a decade later, the roughly 4,100-square-foot, three-bedroom unit is heading to a sealed-bid auction with a reserve price $4.4 million below what he originally paid — a potential 41% discount from its last sale price.Bidding is open now and closes on October 29, though the property remains subject to a prior sale.Perched on the 59th floor of Millennium Tower, the penthouse comes with sweeping views and, according to the listing agent, has barely been lived in since Dell bought it. Notably, the home's oven has apparently never even been turned on.The sale comes at an interesting moment for Dell. His fortune took a $15.1 billion hit this past week as Dell Technologies shares fell amid a broader AI-stock selloff, knocking him down to No. 4 on Forbes' Real-Time Billionaires List. Just days earlier, he had briefly climbed to No. 2 on that same list for the first time. Despite the sharp drop, there's little to suggest the sale is driven by financial necessity — Dell remains one of the wealthiest people in the world.The auction is being handled by Paramount Realty USA in collaboration with SERHANT. Massachusetts. Paramount founder and CEO Misha Haghani acknowledged there's a real possibility a buyer could land a good deal, though he was careful to note that what counts as a "good deal" is ultimately subjective and will come down to how the market responds. Haghani declined to comment on why Dell is selling.This isn't Dell's first eye-catching real estate move. The Dell Technologies founder and CEO previously paid $100.47 million for a penthouse at Manhattan's One57 in 2014, a deal that set records at the time. His willingness to buy — and now sell — trophy properties at steep prices underscores a pattern of high-profile real estate bets that mirror the volatility of his tech fortune, which has swung dramatically in recent weeks alongside the broader AI-driven market turbulence hitting Dell Technologies stock.
Article Summary: Dell Technologies founder and CEO has put his 4,100-square-foot Boston penthouse on the market, a property he purchased a decade ago for $10.9 million. The penthouse offers sweeping city views, luxury finishes, and access to exclusive amenities. The residence reflects Dell’s penchant for high-value real estate investments, complementing his portfolio that includes properties in Texas and Hawaii.

Article Title: Apple Pay may launch in India next month: Report
Article Text:
Apple Pay may launch in India next month: Report

Will Apple Pay support UPI in India

Apple Pay has been in talks with Indian banks

Apple Pay could finally launch in India as early as October, according to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman. In the latest edition of his Power On newsletter, Gurman said Apple is preparing to launch Apple Pay in India “finally” next month. The service is expected to support card payments, while there are also reports that Apple could bring UPI support to the platform. The service was first launched in the US in 2014.Gurman said Apple Pay is expected to support UPI alongside card payments. UPI is India's widely used digital payments system and allows users to make instant payments through participating banks and apps. However, Reuters' recent report about Apple's India plans did not mention UPI as part of the initial rollout.Earlier reports had also suggested that Apple Pay could initially launch without UPI, with support potentially added later.According to Reuters, Axis Bank is expected to be Apple's first major banking partner when Apple Pay launches in India. Apple is reportedly preparing to support Axis Bank credit cards initially. The company is also in discussions with HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank, although commercial agreements with those lenders had not been finalised, according to the report.Apple is expected to add more banks over time through separate agreements with lenders.Apple has reportedly been discussing its India plans with several major banks and payment networks for months. A Bloomberg report in February said Apple was in talks with Axis Bank, HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank, as well as Visa and Mastercard. At the time, Apple Pay was expected to launch around the middle of 2026, but that timeline did not happen.If the latest October timeline is accurate, Apple Pay could soon enter India's established digital payments market, initially with limited banking support before expanding to more lenders.
Article Summary: Apple Pay could finally launch in India as early as October, according to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman. Gurman said Apple is preparing to launch Apple Pay in India ‘finally’ next month. The service is expected to support card payments, while there are also reports that Apple could bring UPI support to the platform.

Article Title: Iran war risk: JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon warns of oil shocks, sticky inflation and higher interest rates
Article Text: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon has warned that the ongoing war in Iran could trigger oil and commodity price shocks, keeping inflation elevated and pushing interest rates higher than current market expectations, Reuters reported.The warning came in his annual letter to shareholders, a day after US President Donald Trump escalated pressure on Iran by threatening to target key infrastructure if the Strait of Hormuz is not reopened."Now, because of the war in Iran, we additionally face the potential for significant ongoing oil and commodity price shocks, along with the reshaping of global supply chains, which may lead to stickier inflation and ultimately higher interest rates than markets currently expect," Dimon said, news agency Reuters quoted as saying.Dimon, who has led JPMorgan for two decades, also highlighted broader geopolitical risks, including the war in Ukraine, tensions in the Middle East and friction with China."The challenges we all face are significant," he added.He said it remains uncertain whether the Iran war will achieve US objectives, while warning that nuclear proliferation remains the biggest risk linked to Iran.Markets have already begun pricing in these risks, with expectations of interest rate cuts this year largely fading amid rising inflation concerns triggered by the conflict.Last week, the benchmark S&P 500 index recorded its worst quarterly performance since 2022, weighed down by rising energy prices and geopolitical uncertainty since late February.Dimon noted that the US economy remains resilient, with consumers continuing to earn and spend, and businesses staying broadly healthy, though signs of weakening have emerged.He cautioned that economic strength has been supported by significant government deficit spending and past stimulus, while infrastructure investment needs continue to grow.At the same time, he pointed to positives such as fiscal stimulus under President Trump's "Big, Beautiful Bill", deregulation policies and rising capital expenditure driven by artificial intelligence.On financial stability, Dimon said the $1.8-trillion private credit market "probably" does not pose a systemic risk, despite investor concerns and recent withdrawals from such funds.However, he warned that in a downturn, losses across leveraged lending could exceed expectations as credit standards have weakened.Private credit markets also lack transparency and rigorous valuation benchmarks, increasing the risk of investor exits if conditions worsen, he said.Separately, Dimon criticised revised US capital rules, including Basel III and GSIB surcharge norms, calling aspects of the proposals "nonsensical" and "very flawed".He said JPMorgan’s GSIB surcharge would fall only to 5.0%, a level he described as “absurd” and “un-American”, arguing it penalises the bank’s scale and performance.
Article Summary: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon warns Iran war could trigger oil and commodity price shocks. He also highlighted broader geopolitical risks, including the war in Ukraine, tensions in the Middle East and friction with China. Dimon criticised revised US capital rules, including Basel III and GSIB surcharge norms, calling aspects of the proposals "nonsensical"

Article Title: How selling Alaska in 1867 was a costly mistake for Russia
Article Text:
Image: Wikipedia

Why Russia agreed to the Alaska purchase

The hidden wealth Russia gave away

Strategic and geopolitical consequences

In 1867, Russia’s decision to sell Alaska to America turned out to be a historic mistake that was to go unnoticed for years to come. The sum paid by the US was only $7,200,000. Although, in the light of the circumstances at the time, it appeared logical, retrospectively, the act looks extremely shortsighted. Russia found itself economically constrained, geographically far away from the region and fearful of its falling into the hands of the British without any compensation. In reality, however, the region had proved immensely valuable both strategically and naturally. Its vast reserves of oil, gold, and natural resources would later transform it into one of the most economically significant territories in the United States.The choice of selling Alaska was based on economic and political reasons. By the middle of the 19th century, the Russian Empire experienced financial difficulties as a result of the expensive Crimean War. It had become increasingly hard for the country to manage such remote and thinly populated areas as Alaska.According to EBSCO , “the Russian-American Company was in decline, and the colony failed to yield any profit”.In addition to this, the lucrative fur trade had declined, making the territory much less economically valuable for the empire.At the same time, Russia was afraid that Britain might capture Alaska in case another war broke out between the two countries. Selling the colony to the friendly United States appeared as a logical step. As the Office of the Historian states, William H. Seward, U.S. Secretary of State, “it was a chance to expand its influence in North America and hinder further growth of Britain”.For Russia, the transaction was a chance to minimise the losses. However, it greatly undervalued the potential of Alaska.Another thing that Russia did not expect was the amount of riches that Alaska possessed. Within several decades after the acquisition, the state saw discoveries of enormous deposits of gold, oil, and other minerals.“Alaska has produced more than 40 million ounces of gold,” according to the US Geological Survey. Furthermore, Alaska is home to some of the world's most significant undeveloped mineral deposits, according to the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) . But even more importantly, the state's oil deposits turned out to be extremely valuable. The Prudhoe Bay oil field was discovered in 1968 and became one of North America's biggest.In retrospect, the amount paid by the Americans, $7.2 million, or two cents per acre, was rather laughable. According to Howard I. Kushner , the deal “robbed Russia of an enormously rich territory, the true value of which would only be recognised in the twentieth century.”In addition to resources, there is the question of strategy and how important Alaska is to the United States from a strategic standpoint. This is a very good place when it comes to defence strategy. It borders on the Arctic Ocean and also happens to be close to Russia.During the period of the Cold War, the Alaskan region became a frontier area for the United States, becoming home to military facilities and warning systems.According to Col. Michael J. Forsyth, U.S. Army, the closeness of Russia and Alaska, only about ninety kilometres apart across the Bering Strait, meant that this region became highly significant to the United States' defence plans.From today's point of view, the strategic location of Alaska makes the state very important to the policies of the U.S. related to the Arctic, energy security, and even environmental policies.Thinking back, what seems clear to us now is that the Russians sold Alaska due to immediate needs rather than future considerations. In order to solve the problem, they lost a valuable resource for Russia.Conclusively, the Alaska Purchase should not have been done as it has had a significant impact that will remain throughout history.
Article Summary: Russia sold Alaska to the U.S. in 1867 for only $7,200,000. However, the region proved immensely valuable both strategically and naturally. Alaska is home to some of the world's most significant undeveloped mineral deposits. The Prudhoe Bay oil field was discovered in 1968.

Article Title: AI data centers are causing 'stress' not just to tech companies, but also private insurers
Article Text:
Massive investments, growing risks



Unique challenges for data centre insurance companies

AI data centers are reportedly putting new pressure on the insurance industry. According to a CNBC report, experts warn that the rapid growth of these projects is becoming a “stress test” not just for tech companies, but also for private insurers and lenders. Consulting firm McKinsey estimates that global spending on data centers could reach $7 trillion by 2030. As costs rise, tech giants are increasingly relying on private equity, private credit and debt to fund these projects. The scale of investments is creating challenges for insurers.“When you put $10 to $20 billion plus in a single location, it creates capacity issues in the marketplace,” said Tom Harper, data center leader at insurance broker Gallagher as quoted in the CNBC report.He added that the sector has been a “real stress test” over the last few years, as insurers struggle to provide coverage for such large and complex projects. While these facilities are seen as high-quality assets, Harper said insuring them has become difficult due to their size and risk concentration.Private data center deals have crossed $10 billion regularly, with some reaching as high as $40 billion. Companies including Nvidia, Microsoft and BlackRock have already taken part in large investment deals.Rajat Rana, partner at Quinn Emanuel Urquhart & Sullivan, described the scale as unprecedented. “We’re talking about trillions of dollars, and almost going back to the same cycle where there’s almost no transparency about the financing structures — the scale is astronomical,” he said. He added that the boom in AI data centers could be “the largest peacetime investment project in human history.”Experts say the way these projects are financed is adding another layer of risk. Much of the funding is happening through complex and less transparent debt structures. Rana warned that this trend feels like “deja vu,” referring to past financial cycles. He said the lack of transparency could create risks for investors, insurers and pension funds.As stated in the CNBC report, data centers offer unique challenges due to their mix of real estate and advanced technology. Insurers are now designing custom policies to manage these risks. However, challenges remain. Large facilities are often located in areas prone to extreme weather, and they store expensive equipment, sometimes even before installation.Another key concern is the mismatch between the lifespan of data centers and the hardware they use. While data centers can last decades, GPUs — the chips powering AI — typically last around seven years. Rana described this as a “GPU debt treadmill,” saying, “This is almost like a treadmill that these AI data centers are running on.”He explained that companies may need to keep raising debt to upgrade infrastructure as technology evolves.
Article Summary: Private data center deals have crossed $10 billion regularly, with some reaching as high as $40 billion. McKinsey estimates that global spending on data centers could reach $7 trillion by 2030. Tech giants are increasingly relying on private equity, private credit and debt to fund these projects.

Article Title: 'Wild witch hunt': Delhi HC refuses to hear FIR plea against ex-judge Yashwant Varma
Article Text:
Varma, who was facing impeachment proceedings, resigned this year on April 9.





NEW DELHI: Delhi high court Monday refused to entertain a plea seeking the registration of an FIR and a probe by an SIT or CBI into the purported discovery of a huge stash of cash last year following a fire at the residence of former Delhi high court judge Yashwant Varma."I'm not entertaining this. This is a wild witch hunt. You have nothing better to do?" Justice Amit Bansal asked, adding that the petitioner, lawyer Ghanshyam Upadhyay, had alternative remedies available in law.HC questioned the locus of the petitioner and asked why he did not approach the trial court with his plea.The petitioner said the incident was "extraordinary" in nature and the lower court "can't do justice to the matter". After the court indicated that it would dismiss the plea, the petitioner withdrew it to consider other legal remedies.The petitioner had earlier approached SC with his plea, which was dismissed in Aug.Amid the row that followed the purported discovery of cash at Varma's residence on March 14, 2025, he was transferred to Allahabad HC.Varma, who was facing impeachment proceedings, resigned this year on April 9. The rare proceedings initiated by LS against Varma were rendered "infructuous" following his resignation.
Article Summary: Varma, who was facing impeachment proceedings, resigned this year on April 9. The rare proceedings initiated by LS against Varma were rendered "infructuous" The petitioner had earlier approached SC with his plea, which was dismissed in Aug.

Article Title: Nanded-Panvel, Nanded-Hadapsar trains get three more coaches each
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





The South Central Railway (SCR) has granted a permanent increase of three coaches each to the Nanded-Panvel and Nanded-Hadapsar Express trains and approved conversion of the Nanded-Mumbai Rajya Rani Express to modern LHB coaches, meeting a long-standing demand of Marathwada passengers.The Nanded-Panvel-Nanded Express (Nos. 17614/17613) and Nanded-Hadapsar-Nanded Express (Nos. 17630/17629) will run with 20 LHB coaches instead of 17, with one additional AC 2-tier, one AC 3-tier and one sleeper coach each on a permanent basis. The revised composition will include two AC 2-tier, six AC 3-tier, six sleeper, four general, one SLR and one guard-cum-divyangjan coach.“The recently received connectivity of Nanded to Western Maharashtra has evoked excellent response. The permanent increase of three coaches is expected to ease heavy waitlists on the Mumbai-Pune corridor,” Rajesh Shinde, chief publicity inspector of SCR’s Nanded division, said.In another upgrade, Nanded-CST Mumbai-Nanded Rajya Rani Express (17611/17612) will run with modern LHB rakes from Nov 4 from Nanded and Nov 5 from Mumbai. The 16-coach LHB composition will include five sleeper, four general, one AC chair car, two AC 3-tier, one AC 2-tier, one first AC and divyangjan-friendly coaches, offering safer and more comfortable travel, railway authorities said.Meanwhile, in a major enforcement action, the Nanded division conducted a mega ticket-checking drive on Sunday from 4.30am to 8pm. Under the supervision of assistant commercial manager Shailesh Kumar Singh, 28 staff checked 29 trains, detecting 669 cases of ticketless travel, irregular travel and unbooked luggage. A total fine of Rs3,45,925 was recovered from the errant travellers.
Article Summary: The South Central Railway (SCR) has granted a permanent increase of three coaches each to the Nanded-Panvel and Nander-Hadapsar Express trains. The Nanded division conducted a mega ticket-checking drive on Sunday from 4.30am to 8pm, detecting 669 cases of ticketless travel.

Article Title: ​FDA seizes another consignment of suspicious sweets in Sambhajinagar
Article Text:
Seized stock of suspicious sweets

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) intensified its “Safe Food Safe Maharashtra” campaign with two separate enforcement operations on Sunday evening, seizing a combined 4,765 kilograms of suspected substandard sweets and Khoya-analog products valued at around Rs7.6 lakh from inter-state tourist buses near Shahnoormiya Dargah Chowk here.The FDA last week seized 1,121kg of suspicious khoya-based sweets transported from Gujarat to the city. Acting on confidential information from Mumbai Intelligence Bureau about large-scale movement of questionable dairy-based confectionery from Gujarat to Marathwada during festival season, a special FDA team mounted surveillance in the travel parking area.In the first operation, the team intercepted two buses arriving from Ahmedabad. From a private tourist bus, the officials recovered 2,079 kilograms of products collectively valued at Rs3.6 lakh and allegedly intended for wholesale distribution in the city.A concurrent check of another private bus at the same location led to the seizure of an additional 1,612 kilograms of assorted sweets worth Rs 2.5 lakh. This first phase alone accounted for 3,691 kilograms valued at Rs5.9 lakh.In the second separate operation conducted the same evening, the team examined another consignment brought by a private bus from Ahmedabad and confiscated 1,074 kilograms of suspect sweets worth Rs1.7 lakh.The seized stock comprised six varieties of sweets, with the condensed milk analogue constituting the largest share at 514 kilograms.Food safety officer Varsha Rode said statutory samples from each variety in both operations have been drawn and dispatched to the designated food testing laboratory for detailed analysis, while the remaining bulk quantities have been sealed and stored at a cold storage facility to preserve their condition pending results.FDA joint commissioner Shrikaant Karkale said public health remains non-negotiable during the festive period. “Once laboratory reports establish violations, stringent prosecution will be initiated under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006,” he said, adding that surprise inspections and intelligence-based actions will continue unabated in the coming days.The FDA has appealed to the traders to source sweets only from licensed manufacturers with proper billing, while urging consumers to remain vigilant about quality and labelling.
Article Summary: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) intensified its “Safe Food Safe Maharashtra’ campaign with two separate enforcement operations on Sunday evening. The FDA last week seized 1,121kg of suspicious khoya-based sweets transported from Gujarat to the city.
